top_comments.text: It also is gonna cost more than an house to run. By the laws of thermodynamics, you cannot just increase output without either some black magic levels of efficiency or some equally expensive input.

top_reply.author: @Delta-007
top_reply.text: No, thermodynamics has nothing to do with it that's not how it works. You have no idea what you're talking about. It's most likely new architecture and better training. More floating point operations used doesn't mean better output, there are lots of variables. In fact if you just increase FLOPs and processing capacity, which i assume you're referring to, i.e more data centers/servers, the performance will plateau and you'll eventually need twice the processing power just to move 1 point on the benchmark score. You don't use all of its processing output when you use it you only use a couple tokens which communicate between themselves, like neurons to generate output.
